newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes hit French public transport in provinces.
newsitem.headline: Strikes hit French public transport in provinces.

text.p: A strike by French public transport drivers hit many cities for a second day on Friday and unions in some cities voted to extend the stoppages, aimed at securing early retirement and shorter working hours.
The strikes disrupted buses, trams and underground Metro railways in cities including Marseille, Montpellier, Dijon, Clermont-Ferrand and Lille.
Unions voted in some cities to prolong the action, originally called for 24 hours on Thursday, until Monday.

Workers in the independent Force Ouvriere, the Communist-led CGT and local unions want a cut in retirement age to 55 and a shorter working week of 35 hours with no pay cut, reckoning the measures would help reduce record employment in France.

In the Mediterranean port of Marseille, for instance, only a fraction of the usual number of buses were running, trams were all blocked and service on the Metro was sporadic. In Dijon, strikers blockaded bus depots.

In some cities, including Lyon and Rennes, workers were back at work after striking on Thursday. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, bus drivers returned to work around midday on Friday after winning a wage hike of 200 francs ($35) a month.

Paris was unaffected by the strikes, as drivers already have benefits the provincial unions are seeking. At the other extreme, public transport in the southwestern city of Toulouse was paralysed by strikes for the 12th day in a row.

"We won't give up the movement...Negotiations have to be nationwide, we're prepared for a long conflict," said Alain Chuffart, a leader of the CGT in Lille, where drivers voted to extend the strike until Monday.
